questions.q: How does the lesson distinguish an AI audit from a financial audit?
options: An AI audit checks whether a system actually operates the way the organization claims and whether its governance controls truly exist, not just the accuracy of numbers
An AI audit only checks the accuracy of financial statements
There is no meaningful difference between the two
An AI audit is always performed by the same team as a financial audit
questions.explain: The lesson frames an AI audit as broader than a financial audit — verifying real operation and controls, not just numeric accuracy.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the six pieces of evidence the lesson says a real AI audit should be able to produce?
options: An access log showing who can reach the model and its training data, matching the approved list
A copy of the company's holiday party photos
The CEO's personal calendar
A list of unrelated competitor products
questions.explain: The access log (tied to Chapter 4's access controls) is one of the six evidence items the lesson names, alongside documentation, risk tier justification, bias testing evidence, monitoring records, and an approval record.

questions.q: What does the lesson say should happen if a required piece of evidence is missing for a high-risk system?
options: That absence itself is a finding — the audit should surface the gap rather than assume good intent fills it
The audit should assume the control exists and move on
The system should be immediately deleted with no further review
Missing evidence is only a problem for low-risk systems
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that a missing evidence item is itself a finding, especially for higher-risk systems.

questions.q: In the lesson's five-step audit structure, what comes right after scoping which systems are in the audit?
options: Requesting the evidence items by name before the audit begins
Immediately firing the system's owner
Publishing the findings to the public before review
Skipping straight to remediation with no evidence review
questions.explain: The five steps are scope, evidence request, walkthrough, gap identification, and findings/remediation, in that order.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what is the practical difference between an internal and an external AI audit?
options: An internal audit proactively catches problems before an external party (regulator, customer, third party) finds them
An external audit is always less thorough than an internal one
Internal audits are optional and never need documentation
External audits are run by the same employees who built the system
questions.explain: The lesson describes internal audits as the proactive check, done on a schedule tied to risk tier, that should catch issues before any external audit does.
